label: Moodles
title: Moodles
lead: Reference for moodle display, intensity tiers, and the player condition indicators mods commonly surface.
bodyHtml:
Status moodle bridge

MoodleRegistry feeds custom entries into vanilla's MoodleManager during its normal refresh pass.

Supply a sprite or an existing vanilla icon ID, a display name, a description, a valid background intensity, and an important choice for the main or side row. Resolve localized text before passing it in; vanilla uses these strings directly.

When to add a moodle

Use a moodle when the player needs visible feedback about a custom status effect. Keep it lightweight. The normal pattern is to call MoodleRegistry.AddMoodle(...) each update while the condition is active; CUCoreLib keeps it visible briefly and avoids duplicate spam for the same warning.

MoodleRegistry.AddMoodle(
        1,
        someLoadedImageAsset,
        "Lead Poisoning",
        "You're feeling a bit woozy and fatigued...",
        critical: false,
        chippedOnly: false
    );

Disappear together with a vanilla moodle

Vanilla rebuilds its moodles every 0.5 unscaled seconds and reevaluates each condition. It does not give each moodle an expiration timer. Queued entries instead expire after their last refresh, so matching the interval alone cannot guarantee simultaneous disappearance.

For a moodle tied to another condition, register a callback once during plugin startup and evaluate the same condition there. Return null when inactive. Both entries are then evaluated in the same vanilla refresh, with no queued hold time. Keep these callbacks free of gameplay changes; they are evaluated for both rows.

// Declare in your mod, then call RegisterMoodles() once from Awake().
public sealed class FocusMoodleStatus : BodyStatus { }

private static void RegisterMoodles()
{
    MoodleRegistry.RegisterBody<FocusMoodleStatus>((body, status) =>
    {
        // The same condition used by vanilla's focused moodle.
        if (!body.alive || body.focusedLevel <= 0f) return null;

        return new StatusMoodleDefinition
        {
            Intensity = 8,
            Icon = "focused",
            Name = "Custom focus effect",
            Description = "Active while the vanilla focused moodle is active.",
            Important = true
        };
    });
}

Import CUCoreLib.Data and CUCoreLib.Registries. For limb-specific conditions, use RegisterLimb<TStatus> with a LimbStatus. The definition also accepts IconSprite for custom images.

AddMoodle parameters/fields

ParameterTypeWhat it does
intensityintPicks the vanilla moodle background tier. Use the intensity table below for the visual mapping.
iconSpriteSprite icon.
iconIdstringString-based overload only. Don't use, unless the icon already exists in MoodleManager.icons.
namestringMouseover title text shown on the moodle. Can be localized.
descriptionstringMouseover description text shown in the hover/details UI. Can be localized.
criticalboolAdds the vanilla critical overlay glow. This is separate from the intensity number.
chippedOnlyboolIf true, the moodle will only be displayed when the player has a chip.
importantboolIf false, the moodle will be displayed in the unimportant hidden-ish section to the right.
keystringOptional stable queue key. Supply this when a moodle changes severity over time. (Where you only want one moodle with the same key active at a time.)
holdSecondsfloatUnscaled seconds before a queued entry expires after its last refresh. The default is 0.5f, matching vanilla's refresh interval; removal occurs on the next UI rebuild. Explicit values remain supported (minimum 0.05f). Rebuild dependent mods to pick up the new optional-argument default.

If you want animated icons instead, AddAnimatedMoodle(...) swaps the icon argument for animationId but otherwise follows the same parameter meanings.

The intensity value picks the same vanilla background frame used by the base game.

IntensityVisualNotes
0Lowest standard tier.
1Low warning tier.
2Moderate warning tier.
3Strong warning tier.
4Used by minor positive/sleep moodles.
5Higher positive or special tier.
6Strong positive or special tier.
7Special positive standard tier. (Life Support)
8Special last-tier background used by rare moodles. (Last Stand)
critical: trueCritical is an overlay behavior, not a separate intensity number
